title: An 8 mm sample (εr = 2.2, tan δ = 0.01) in WR-90 between 10 mm of empty guide each side: εr and μr read back from the solved S by Nicolson–Ross–Weir
source: The sample's material, εr = 2.2(1 − 0.01j) = 2.2 − 0.022j, μr = 1, which the NRW inversion (A. M. Nicolson and G. F. Ross, IEEE Trans. Instrum. Meas. IM-19(4), 1970; W. B. Weir, Proc. IEEE 62(1), 1974) recovers exactly from the exact TE10 cascade (emcraft_theory::nrw's tests)

quantities.reason: second-order elements of 3 mm: the solved S21's phase is off by about 0.01° and S11 by about 1e-4, which the inversion carries into εr′ at about 1e-4 relative
as at 8 GHz; the elements are fewer per wavelength, so the error is largest here (about 2e-4)
the loss is read from |T| over 8 mm (about 0.03 dB): 1 % of it is 2e-4 in εr″
μr comes from the wave impedance (1 + Γ)/(1 − Γ), most sensitive to S11's error: about 2e-4 here
